I got the brawler and find it isn't great. It's pretty average as an off-roader.

Its only RWD. That might be a glitch, or it could be intentional as the real life counterpart is only RWD.

Silent except for the hum

that always hums in the wall.

All this electricity can't be good for us.

The dogs pant and roll around

on the stained

crushed carpet floor.

I pet the small one and it's like she's

not even there.

Like she's a leaf

waiting to click away down the sidewalk.

I haven't written poetry in months

but I thought this silence

was too nice to interrupt.

The creaking, humming walls

and the restless

black dog

and the little white one with bones

like leaves.

And outside

the lawnmowers coughing to life

after 9 months

of near death.

Cars grip the pavement

instead of helplessly grasping

at snow.

In their element and motorcycles

sounding off in the distance

reclaiming their asphalt

and dead grass

floating away with a warm breeze.

A springtime sadness, or maybe

it's always been there

lurking behind every day.

With the sun out

and no grey clouds

It's easier to see.

Soft Saturdays are meant to reflect

and tomorrow is Easter

when dead Gods rise

so maybe there's hope

for dead men.
I wrote this the day before Easter.

I really like the idea you're trying to get across, contrasting the previous winter months with the new springtime. However, I only begin to see this idea emerge about halfway through the poem. The part about the dogs and walls seems out of place. Something to focus on in the future is keeping a single idea that is displayed throughout the whole of the poem, or a fluid story who's purpose remains constant.

I tried to have the overlapping theme be change. An almost resistance to it, yet it being an unstoppable force. The dogs bones like leaves were supposed to represent fall, the black dog was to represent my restlessness. I may have missed the mark, though. Thanks for the critique!
